# QS-CFW-7185-40 Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (4340)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-7185-40

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (4340) produced at Plant P2. It applies to all incoming forgings, in-process blanks, and finished blanks identified as CFW-7185-40. The objective is to ensure material, dimensional, and hardness requirements meet downstream machining and performance expectations.

Background and rationale
- CFW-7185-40 is a 4340 alloy crankshaft blank that must meet tight hardness and bore tolerance requirements to control machining performance, crankshaft balance, and fatigue life after subsequent heat treatment and finish operations. The specified hardness range limits the amount of hardenability and work hardening introduced during forging and prior handling. Bore dimensional control ensures fitment accuracy in downstream operations and alignment of main bearing journals. Maximum forging weight is controlled to ensure handling equipment and heat treatment loads remain within certified capacities for plant P2 tooling and furnaces.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the controlled attributes and acceptance criteria for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40).

| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Hardness range | The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40) is 39-42 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40) is ±0.07 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40) is 117.8 kg. |

Inspection method
- Material verification
  - Verify raw material certification and traceability for each heat lot against purchase documentation and mill test report. Confirm alloy designation matches 4340 and associated chemical compliance per incoming material procedures. Record material heat identifiers with the production lot record.
- Visual inspection
  - Inspect each blank for surface discontinuities, laps, and forging defects using daylight and clean surface conditions. Remove light scale if necessary to reveal surface indications before acceptance evaluation. Document any visible defects on the inspection record and photograph defects that are unclear or borderline for review.
- Dimensional inspection (bores and critical features)
  - Establish a dedicated inspection setup for measuring bore diameters using calibrated measuring equipment appropriate for the feature size and geometry. Verify operator competence and calibration status are recorded on the measurement log. Measure the bore(s) and record the nominal measurement and deviation. Acceptance is based on meeting the bore diameter tolerance.
  - Example: If the measured deviation is within the bore diameter tolerance for the part, accept the blank and proceed to process control records. If the deviation exceeds tolerance, follow the nonconformance handling procedure below.
- Hardness inspection
  - Perform hardness testing on specified locations on the blank using a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC measurement. Ensure surface preparation meets testing equipment requirements to obtain reliable readings. Record individual hardness readings and the location for traceability. Acceptance requires the measured hardness to fall within the specified hardness range.
  - Example: If hardness measurements are within the hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40), log results in the inspection report and release the part for downstream operations.
- Weight verification
  - Confirm forging weight by comparing shop floor scale records against the maximum forging weight requirement. Record the measured weight on the production traveler.
  - Example: If the measured forging weight is equal to or less than the maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40), continue normal processing. If the measured weight exceeds the maximum forging weight, initiate the nonconformance handling steps below.

Inspection records to keep
- Material heat certificate and traceability record for each lot.
- Visual inspection log including defect descriptions and photographs for atypical findings.
- Dimensional inspection log showing nominal measurements, deviations, measurement locations, and inspector identification.
- Hardness test log showing test locations, individual readings, equipment identification, and calibration status.
- Forging weight record from the shop floor scale with operator initials.
- Final disposition record for each blank indicating accept, rework, or scrap, with justification and reviewer signature.
- Retain inspection records in the document control system according to Plant P2 retention policy and make available to quality audits and customer requests.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any blank failing to meet the requirements in the Requirements table shall be clearly identified as nonconforming and segregated from conforming inventory to prevent unintended use. Use visual tags and physical separation at the point of discovery.
- Initial containment and notification
  - The inspector records the nonconformance on the nonconformance report and notifies the production lead and quality engineer. Provide complete measurement data, photographs, and material traceability to support disposition.
- Disposition options
  - Accept: Only allowed if an approved engineering deviation exists. The deviation must reference the affected attribute and provide clear justification and approval by authorized engineering personnel.
  - Rework: If the nonconformance is judged remediable (for example, machining to correct bore within tolerance), document the rework instructions, responsible party, and reinspection requirements. Reinspection must confirm compliance with the original requirement before release.
  - Scrap: When rework is not feasible and no deviation is approved, the blank is to be scrapped. Document scrap reason and record material disposition.
- Example disposition scenarios
  - Example: A blank exhibits hardness below the hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40). If engineering authorizes reheat and quench corrective action, the reheat process must be documented and the blank requalified via hardness testing and dimensional inspection before release. If no corrective action is authorized, scrap the blank and record the decision.
  - Example: A bore measurement deviates beyond the bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40). If machining allowance remains and rework can restore the feature to within tolerance without compromising part integrity, document the rework and reinspection. If not, disposition as scrap or request an engineering deviation.
- Corrective action and records
  - For all nonconformances, initiate corrective action as appropriate to prevent recurrence. Document root cause analysis, containment actions, corrective steps, responsible owners, and completion evidence in the corrective action record. Link corrective actions to the affected production lot and retain records for audit.
- Escalation
  - For production impacts or repeated nonconformances with the same characteristic, escalate to plant quality management for further review and potential process changes.

Notes
- All measurement equipment used for acceptance testing must be calibrated and traceable. Calibration records are maintained with inspection equipment documentation.
- Any approved engineering deviations or special dispositions must be recorded and attached to the lot’s quality records.
